questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Felt very easy and natural if you just followed the instructions made available by the host university and KU

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The host university sent informational mails and so on but you had to figure out lots of things on your own - such as how to navigate on their online platforms, which campus you were enrolled into and when and where the classes took place. But they were always available to help you if you reached out to the host university with questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used Airbnb for housing which has been a great experience. The communication were good, the people I rented from were so helpfull and welcoming. If any problems occurred they sorted it out immediately.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is the best way to experience the culture and you get such a unique connection to the city and your neighbourhood.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process were okay. You just have to fill out all of the forms online, which is sent to you by mail.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
The contact person from the host university were available for helping you in the registration process. 
But there where also guides and templates that were very helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
The hardest thing about registration at the host university was to make your schedule work.
All the classes where overlapping - but it is easy to modify it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time and read every e-mail. The help and answer is there.

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Digital Society, Languages of The Media, Corporate Communication and Coding for Computational Social Science.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the courses I took were good and so were the professors. But especially Digital Society and Languages of The Media were great and the teaching was amazing.

questions.answer: Erasmus has a lot of activities available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There a a lot to do and explore inn the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Weekend trips to other cities and to visit all the museums!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The locals were super friendly and helpfull.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The atmosphere is more open and therefore it is easier to connect with the local. It helps being curious and sweet towards everyone you meet.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The local students talked in class while the professor were teaching - this were challenging to get used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their kindness, warmth and open mind. And the fact that they never rushed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Check up on all the information for enrolment. 
Choose classes that you find interesting. 
Enjoy it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Professor Christopher Anderson is one of the best teachers I ever had! Pick a class with him as professor.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and became friends with.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To challenge ones independence in a new city and culture.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
